# Objectives

BLM assumptions evaluated (two paired scenarios)

-   **Carbonate charge balance**

    -   Baseline: Closed system, measured DIC as input

    -   Perturbed: Open system, no DIC input, alkalinity estimated by charge balance (assuming in equilibrium with atmospheric partial pressure)

-   **Humic acid fraction of DOC**

    -   Baseline: HA = 10% (suggested by the BLM manual)

    -   Perturbed: HA = 80%

# 1. Data Organization

We will merge BLM output variables from the baseline conditions (closed system + HA 10%) and the perturbed scenarios (open system + HA 10% and closed system + HA 80%) which are currently organized into separate tabs within the Bioavailability Master Spreadsheet.

First, we'll set the working directory

```{r}
setwd("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/1. Spatial Assessment/Data/Spatial Assessment of Bioavailability Project/6. Sensitivity analyses")
```

Next, we'll will import each dataset as it's own object

```{r}
library(readxl)

ha_10_cs <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/1. Spatial Assessment/Data/Spatial Assessment of Bioavailability Project/5. Statistical data analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean_3.xlsx", 
    sheet = "HA 10% Closed System")

ha_10_os <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/1. Spatial Assessment/Data/Spatial Assessment of Bioavailability Project/4. Exploratory data analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean_2.xlsx", 
    sheet = "HA 10% Open System")

ha_80_cs <- read_excel("C:/Users/q4q/OneDrive - Oak Ridge National Laboratory/Research/Bioavailability Project/1. Spatial Assessment/Data/Spatial Assessment of Bioavailability Project/4. Exploratory data analysis/Bioavailability_Master_Spreadsheet_Clean_2.xlsx", 
    sheet = "HA 80% Closed System")

# Note: only our baseline condition (ha_10_cs) has the Typology variable
```

Now we'll create new columns in each of these datasets called Scenario and label them as either:

-   ha_10_cs

-   ha_10_os

-   ha_80_cs

```{r}
ha_10_cs$Scenario <- "HA 10% Closed System"
ha_10_os$Scenario <- "HA 10% Open System"
ha_80_cs$Scenario <- "HA 80% Closed System"

# Make it the first column
library(dplyr)

ha_10_cs <- ha_10_cs %>% relocate(Scenario, .before = 1)
ha_10_os <- ha_10_os %>% relocate(Scenario, .before = 1)
ha_80_cs <- ha_80_cs %>% relocate(Scenario, .before = 1)

# Check
unique(ha_10_cs$Scenario)
unique(ha_10_os$Scenario)
unique(ha_80_cs$Scenario)
```

Before we merge the datasets, we need to add the variable Typology to ha_10_os and ha_80_cs since currently only ha_10_cs contains the variable

```{r}
library(dplyr)

typology_lookup <- ha_10_cs %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Typology) %>%
  distinct()

ha_10_os <- ha_10_os %>%
  left_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID")

ha_80_cs <- ha_80_cs %>%
  left_join(typology_lookup, by = "Sample_ID")

# Sanity check that Typology was correctly assigned to each Sample_ID (should be 0)
missing_in_os <- setdiff(ha_10_os$Sample_ID, ha_10_cs$Sample_ID)
missing_in_80 <- setdiff(ha_80_cs$Sample_ID, ha_10_cs$Sample_ID)

missing_in_os
missing_in_80
```

Now we'll merge these into one dataset called dat_long by stacking them vertically and ensuring variables (columns) line up. Since ha_10_os does not have the variable DIC, these values will be left blank

```{r}
library(dplyr)

dat_long <- bind_rows(
  ha_10_cs,
  ha_10_os,
  ha_80_cs
)

View(dat_long)
```

Define ID and grouping columns

```{r}
# String of names
id_cols <- c("Sample_ID", "Typology", "Scenario")
```

# 2. Sensitivity calculations

Calculate a delta (difference in baseline from alternate scenario), percent change (or difference between the two), and log10 difference.

First, we'll create 2 small tables with only the two scenarios to compare:

-   Carbonate assumptions SA table will be called dic_sa

-   HA assumptions SA table will be called ha_sa

## A. Carbonate Assumptions

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

dic_sa <- dat_long %>%
  # Keep only HA 10% scenarios we need
  filter(Scenario %in% c("HA 10% Closed System", "HA 10% Open System")) %>%
  
  # Make a short scenario label to avoid spaces/% in column names
  mutate(Scenario_short = if_else(
    Scenario == "HA 10% Open System", "Open", "Closed"
  )) %>%
  
  # Keep only the columns we need
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Typology, Scenario_short, all_of(response_vars)) %>%
  
  # Put Open and Closed side-by-side
  pivot_wider(
    names_from  = Scenario_short,
    values_from = all_of(response_vars),
    names_sep   = "_"
  )

# Preview
head(dic_sa)
```

### i. Delta

Calculate the change in Closed vs. Open carbonate system

```{r}
# Create an empty table where results will be stored
dic_delta <- dic_sa %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Typology)

# Loop a function across all rows and store results in the above table
for(v in response_vars){
  dic_delta[[paste0("delta_", v)]] <- 
    dic_sa[[paste0(v, "_Open")]] - dic_sa[[paste0(v, "_Closed")]]
}

# Check table
head(dic_delta)
```

### ii. Percent Change

Percentage of delta

```{r}
# Create an empty table where results will be stored
dic_pct <- dic_sa %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Typology)

# Loop a function across all rows and store results in the above table
for (v in response_vars) {

  open_val   <- dic_sa[[paste0(v, "_Open")]]
  closed_val <- dic_sa[[paste0(v, "_Closed")]]

  dic_pct[[paste0("pct_", v)]] <- ifelse(
    !is.na(closed_val) & closed_val != 0,
    (open_val - closed_val) / closed_val * 100,
    NA_real_
  )
}

# Check table
head(dic_pct)
```

### iii. Log Response Ratio

Calculated as the difference in log base 10 in response variables from the baseline (closed system) to that of the perturbed scenario (open system)

```{r}
# Create an empty table where results will be stored
dic_dlog10 <- dic_sa %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Typology)

# Loop a function across all rows and store results in the above table
for(v in response_vars){
  open_val   <- dic_sa[[paste0(v, "_Open")]]
  closed_val <- dic_sa[[paste0(v, "_Closed")]]

  dic_dlog10[[paste0("dlog10_", v)]] <- ifelse(
    !is.na(open_val) & !is.na(closed_val) & open_val > 0 & closed_val > 0,
    log10(open_val) - log10(closed_val),
    NA_real_
  )
}

# Check table
dic_dlog10
```

### iv. Summary Statistics

Mean, median, and interquartile range of the log response ratio by variable

```{r}
# Create an empty summary table
dic_pct_summary <- data.frame(
  Variable = response_vars,
  Mean     = NA_real_,
  Median   = NA_real_,
  IQR      = NA_real_
)

# Loop over each variable and store the results in the above table
for (i in seq_along(response_vars)) {

  v <- response_vars[i]
  vals <- dic_pct[[paste0("pct_", v)]]

  dic_pct_summary$Mean[i]   <- mean(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  dic_pct_summary$Median[i] <- median(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  dic_pct_summary$IQR[i]    <- IQR(vals, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Check table
head(dic_pct_summary)
```

### v. Plot Summary

```{r}
plot_pct <- dic_pct_summary %>%
  arrange(Median) %>%                # order from most negative to most positive
  mutate(Variable = factor(Variable, levels = Variable))

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(plot_pct, aes(y = Variable)) +
  geom_col(aes(x = Median), fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_errorbarh(
    aes(
      xmin = Median - IQR / 2,
      xmax = Median + IQR / 2
    ),
    height = 0.25
  ) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40") +
  labs(
    x = "Median percent change (Open vs Closed)",
    y = NULL,
    title = "Sensitivity of model outputs to carbonate system assumption",
    subtitle = "Bars = median; error bars ≈ IQR"
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

### vii. Normality Checks \***re-visit\***

By Shapiro-Wilk method to determine what type of paired test to conduct

```{r}
# Create an empty results table
shapiro_results <- data.frame(
  Variable = response_vars,
  W = NA_real_,
  p_value = NA_real_,
  n = NA_integer_
)

# Run the stats for each variable and store the results in the table above
for (i in seq_along(response_vars)) {

  v <- response_vars[i]
  vals <- dic_pct[[paste0("pct_", v)]]

  # Remove NA values
  vals_clean <- vals[!is.na(vals)]

  shapiro_results$n[i] <- length(vals_clean)

  # Shapiro–Wilk requires at least 3 observations
  if (length(vals_clean) >= 3) {
    test <- shapiro.test(vals_clean)
    shapiro_results$W[i] <- test$statistic
    shapiro_results$p_value[i] <- test$p.value
  }
}

# Check results
summary(shapiro_results)
```

Check them after log-transformations

### viii. Plots by Scenario

Using their log concentrations

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)


plot_dat <- dat_long %>%
  filter(Scenario %in% c("HA 10% Closed System", "HA 10% Open System")) %>%
  dplyr::select(Sample_ID, Scenario, all_of(response_vars)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(response_vars),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Metal = case_when(
      grepl("Zn", Variable) ~ "Zn",
      grepl("Cu", Variable) ~ "Cu",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )

# Check
table(plot_dat$Scenario)
table(plot_dat$Variable)[1:5]
head(plot_dat)
```

Faceted violin plot of concentration by Scenario and Species

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Zinc
zn_dat <- plot_dat %>% filter(Metal == "Zn")

ggplot(zn_dat, aes(x = Value, y = Variable, fill = Scenario)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, scale = "width", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  labs(
    title = "Zn response variables by scenario (HA 10%)",
    x = "Value",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw()

# Copper
cu_dat <- plot_dat %>% filter(Metal == "Cu")

ggplot(cu_dat, aes(x = Value, y = Variable, fill = Scenario)) +
  geom_violin(trim = FALSE, scale = "width", position = position_dodge(width = 0.8)) +
  labs(
    title = "Cu response variables by scenario (HA 10%)",
    x = "Value",
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw()

```

### ix. Pairwise Comparisons

Since all variables don't pass the Normality test, we'll use the Wilcox signed-rank to compute pairwise comparisons
